query: How can we improve incident resolution efficiency?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing incidents from short_description gives a genuine grouping axis for resolution efficiency analysis. Values (printer_related, network_connectivity, software_system) are sound readings of the source descriptions.

per_column.name: issue_complexity
per_column.rationale: Complexity is a useful axis for prioritization and efficiency modeling. However, groundedness is shaky: 'Unable to connect to the database' -> medium is defensible, but rating most printer issues 'low' is an inference the terse text only weakly supports. It is a plausible but partly asserted judgment.

per_column.name: assigned_technician_id
per_column.rationale: This is essentially redundant with the existing assigned_to original column, offering little new analytical leverage. Values are also not derivable from the sampled source text (short_description/timestamps); they appear copied from an original field, so grounding in the shown evidence is weak.

per_column.name: required_action_type
per_column.rationale: Action type (repair, replacement, troubleshooting) is a useful new axis for resolution workflow analysis. Values are reasonable inferences from the described issue, though for terse descriptions like 'printer not working' the specific action is somewhat assumed.

per_column.name: technician_match_efficiency
per_column.rationale: A technician-suitability flag is directly relevant to the efficiency query. But the true/false values are not supportable from the source text, which contains no skill/matching information; the flag appears invented, and NULLs aside, the assertions are ungrounded.

per_column.name: repeat_issue_pattern
per_column.rationale: Identifying repeat/recurring issues is genuinely useful for efficiency. Recurrence could in principle be derived from duplicate descriptions, but the per-row true/false assignments are not clearly warranted by the isolated source text shown and read as asserted flags.

judge.rationale: Most added columns provide genuine new axes (category, action type, complexity, repeat/match flags) relevant to improving resolution efficiency. assigned_technician_id is largely redundant with the existing assigned_to column. Groundedness is mixed: category and action_type are sound readings of the description text, but issue_complexity, technician_match_efficiency, and repeat_issue_pattern assert judgments the terse source text does not clearly support, indicating hallucination risk.
